sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Radiative Forcing**: The measurement of the capacity of a gas or other forcing agent to affect the energy balance of the Earth-atmosphere system.
• **Tipping Points**: Critical thresholds that, when exceeded, lead to large and often irreversible changes in the state of the system (e.g., collapse of West Antarctic Ice Sheet).
• **Feedback Loops**: Positive feedback mechanisms (e.g., Albedo effect reduction due to melting ice) accelerate warming beyond initial anthropogenic forcing.
• **Key Metric**: 1.5°C vs 2.0°C threshold as defined by IPCC Special Report on Global Warming.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **IPCC Assessment Reports**: The gold standard for scientific consensus on climate impacts.
• **NAPCC (India)**: National Action Plan on Climate Change comprising 8 national missions.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Common But Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR) conflict, climate finance gap.
• **Solutions**: Nature-based Solutions (NbS), Climate-resilient agriculture, Carbon sequestration.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'H-O-T-S' (Impacts)
• **Decoded Meaning**: H-Hydrological (floods/droughts), O-Oceanic (acidification/sea-level), T-Temperature (heatwaves/glaciers), S-Socio-economic (migration/health).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses 'Ocean Acidification' with 'Global Warming'. Acidification is a direct chemical consequence of CO2 absorption, independent of temperature rise.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Climate Justice' when discussing the disproportionate impact of climate change on the Global South.

keyTakeaways: Climate change impacts are non-linear and exhibit significant regional variability.
The cryosphere and oceans act as critical indicators of planetary health.
Adaptation and Mitigation must be integrated into national development planning to ensure long-term sustainability.
